comments.body:
Would use `appId` and `apiKey`:

Do not have to remember that "application id" is named "applicationID" (uppercase I and D). A bit like the mighty getElementByID (took me some time to correct my typing when using it).

Do not have to remember the upper case `APIK` token.

About preventing people to put an "admin key" inside a webpage: we already warn them everywhere and we still get issues about it. I am not sure naming it "searchOnlyAPIKey" would help. People putting sensitive data inside a web page will still do it.

We already document "appId" and "apiKey" inside the [client](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-client-js#browserify-webpack) and [helper](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js#example) (and yes I wrote those examples).

Do we really need to introduce named parameters here? I like the way the JS API client & helper are using a mix of mandatory parameters & optional parameters.

Right now, most API clients are using `applicationId` and `apiKey`. I understand your point with `searchAPIKey` but the mixed camelCase naming makes it complex.

I'll replace with `appId` and `apiKey`, I'm ok with that as long as this is consistent with our other libraries.

@redox: We'll have three mandatory arguments (appId, apiKey, indexName) and a few optional ones. Seems better to provide named parameters here, for readability.
